failure_modes.cause: Back Pressure Regulator (BPR) set at 1.5 bar is insufficient to suppress vapor pressure of solvent at 60°C (estimated P_vap ~0.8-1.0 bar), leading to phase change and flow instability.
failure_modes.mitigation: Increase BPR setting to minimum 2.5 bar (P_vap + dP + 1.0 bar safety margin) and verify solvent vapor pressure data at 60°C.

failure_modes.cause: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution often generates tarry oligomers; low Reynolds number (Re=13) laminar flow in 0.75 mm ID tubing reduces shear forces, allowing particulates to settle and accumulate over long residence times (15 min).
failure_modes.mitigation: Implement inline filtration (0.45 µm) before the reactor and schedule periodic back-flushing or solvent-only purge cycles every 4 hours.

failure_modes.cause: Single-stage EAS reactions can be exothermic; if the quench stream fails or mixes poorly with the hot (60°C) product stream, unreacted electrophile may continue reacting or decompose, potentially causing pressure spikes or hazardous byproduct formation.
failure_modes.mitigation: Validate quench mixing efficiency using a fast colorimetric indicator reaction and install a thermal runaway detection sensor post-quench.

single_points_of_failure: BPR valve failure (stuck open) leading to solvent boiling
Inline filter blockage causing upstream pressure buildup
validation_experiments: Run solvent-only at 60°C and 1.5 bar BPR for 2 hours; monitor for pressure oscillations or flow rate drops indicating cavitation/boiling.
Perform a 'worst-case' fouling test by running a concentrated model reaction mixture for 10 residence times; measure pressure drop increase across the reactor coil.
Conduct a quench failure simulation by stopping the quench feed while maintaining reaction feed; monitor temperature and pressure rise for 5 minutes to assess safety margin.
